title: South Korea's PIPC announces three months of intensive management as reported breaches reach 1,019 in January to October 2026
date_note: Herald Business's articles of 27 November report the commission's briefing that day; the pages give no earlier day.
geo_basis: the commission briefed at the Government Seoul Complex, as Herald Business states; pin at Seoul
summary: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission announced three months of intensive management starting next month, working with the Ministry of Science and ICT, the Financial Services Commission and the National Intelligence Service, Herald Business reports. Reported breaches in the public and private sectors were 307 in 2024, 447 last year and 1,019 in January to October 2026, of which 271 in the public sector and 748 in enterprises.
plain: Korea's data protection regulator will run three months of intensive management from next month. Herald Business reports 1,019 reported breaches in January to October 2026, against 447 last year.
exec: The commission will inspect high-risk companies urgently and says it will strictly investigate and penalise breaches that could have been prevented, Herald Business reports.
action: As the commission urges, companies should enforce multi-factor authentication on key accounts, verify API authentication and remove departed, unused, shared and test accounts; public bodies should check recipients before sending documents.

evidence.quote: 실제로 민간·공공 부문 개인정보 유출은 2024년 307건, 지난해 447건, 올해(1~10월) 1019건 등으로 급증하는 추세다.
올해 개인정보 유출은 중앙행정기관, 지자체, 대학 등 공공 부문에서 271건, 소상공인과 개인사업자·중소기업을 포함한 기업에서 748건 발생했다.

validation.note: Herald Business and edaily each report the commission's briefing with 1,019 reports in January to October 2026; the commission's own release was not read.

review.note: Compared figures, partners, advice against both Herald Business articles; single_source correct
